entries.m: the unconquerable; a very hard stone, sometimes wrongly the loadstone or magnet
entries.n: From Greek, 'the unconquerable'. It has now become 'diamond', the hardest known stone; old writers erroneously used it for the loadstone.

entries.m: devoted themselves, given themselves up to
entries.n: 'Addicted' now usually means given up to some bad habit, but it was not so restricted formerly.

entries.m: to bind by oath, solemnly entreat
simple wonder, astonishment, whether with approval or disapproval

entries.n: Only used once in the Authorised Version.

entries.m: to inform, give notice, generally without reference to time
entries.n: Like the French word, which an old dictionary explains as 'to informe, certifie'.
Occurs only once in the Bible; the translators took it from the Geneva version. Now seldom used.
